The start and finish area is in the Hufeisen parking lot in the forest between the districts of Geißlitz, Großenhausen and Lützel. As part of the Main-Kinzig-Challenge, the race is an important scoring event in the region’s largest running series.
course_highlights: Start and finish in the Hufeisen parking lot in the forest
Run through the forest areas between Geißlitz, Großenhausen and Lützel
Family-friendly atmosphere with strong local participation
additional: The Summer Night Run is part of the Main-Kinzig-Challenge, a running series with seven scoring events. The event attracts several hundred participants each year and provides certificates and results lists via Raceresult.

name: 401. Malá cena Monaka
location: Restaurace Monako, Slatiňany, Pardubický kraj, Czech Republic
description: The Small Monaco Cup is a traditional running race held in Slatiňany in the Pardubice Region. The race is part of the long-standing history of running events organized by the KRB Chrudim club and gives athletes the opportunity to test themselves on interesting courses. It is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to experience a high-quality sporting event in pleasant surroundings.

name: Běh olympijského dne
description: The Olympic Run is a traditional sporting event organized by the Czech Olympic Committee and held in Zlín as part of Olympic Day. The run brings together different generations and levels of runners, from children to adults, and promotes Olympic values such as friendship, fair play, and respect. Participants can choose from shorter or longer routes, and the race is complemented by sporting and educational activities. The entry fee helps support children’s participation in sport through the Czech Olympic Foundation. The event is open to everyone who wants to enjoy the pleasure of being active and support a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Zlín
description: The Olympic Run in Zlín is a traditional sporting event held at the Youth Stadium. The race offers a classic five-kilometre course on a tartan track for adults, as well as several shorter children’s races. The event supports sports activities for children from socially disadvantaged families, with part of the entry fee donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration takes place online, and the race starts at 18:00, with the start broadcast on Czech Radio.

name: Olympijský běh - Bakov nad Jizerou
location: Bakov nad Jizerou, Central Bohemian Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Bakov nad Jizerou is a traditional running race featuring a flat loop that runs partly along a dirt track and a meadow beside the Jizera River, with the final section on an inline skating track. The race is open to adults and children, with children’s races over 500 and 1,000 metres. The 5 km adult race starts at 18:00 and is held under the auspices of Czech Radio. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online only; it will not be possible to register on site.

name: Olympijský běh - Bedřichov
description: The Olympic Run in Bedřichov is the largest running event in the Czech Republic and kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the country. The race takes place in the picturesque Jizera Mountains, on a 5 km course. The main category starts at 18:00 by the stadium in Bedřichov. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate the spirit of sport and Olympic values.

name: Olympijský běh - Brloh
description: The Olympic Run in Brloh is a popular regional running race. It is open to a wide range of ages, from children to seniors, and offers courses for both adults and children. The adult course is 5 km long and runs through the picturesque village along a stream, with a turnaround at the oak tree. The children’s races take place on a loop around the football pitch. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Brno
description: The Olympic Run in Brno is a Gold Race held on the meadow by the Komec sports complex in Brno-Komárov. The race offers 5 km and 10 km courses for adults, as well as 400 m and 800 m children’s races by age category. The event celebrates Olympic Day with a running and sports programme. The main race starts at 18:00 and will be started live on Czech Radio. Registration is online only, and part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Chip timing, a changing room, baggage storage and toilets are available for participants.

name: Olympijský běh - Budyně nad Ohří
description: The Olympic Run in Budyně nad Ohří is a traditional sporting event held at the T.J. Sokol Budyně nad Ohří tennis courts. The 5.8 km main race runs across fields, through a small forest and over a gentle hill, on a mix of asphalt, field tracks and forest paths. Children can take part in 400 m and 1,000 m races in the safe surroundings of the tennis courts. The event is part of Olympic Day, which promotes sporting values and friendship, and also supports the Czech Olympic Foundation in helping children take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Bystřice pod Hostýnem
location: Městský park Zahájené, Bystřice pod Hostýnem, Zlín Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Bystřice pod Hostýnem is a new addition to the running calendar. It takes place in the picturesque Zahájené town park, which combines nature with an urban atmosphere. The route is mostly on firm park paths, with short sections of slightly unpaved surface, and is suitable for experienced runners as well as families with children. During the race, participants can enjoy greenery, mature trees and peaceful parts of the park, with no significant elevation changes. The event is both a sporting and social gathering, with an accompanying program, refreshments and opportunities to cheer along the course. The entry fee supports the Czech Olympic Foundation, which helps children take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Čelákovice
description: The Olympic Run in Čelákovice is a traditional running race, with its fifth edition taking place in 2026. The race offers two adult distances, 5 km and 10 km, on flat routes along the Elbe River, with beautiful views and interesting landmarks such as the railway bridge, St. Wenceslas Chapel, and the courtyard of the Municipal Museum. Children can take part in shorter races from 200 m to 1,500 m, which also pass through the Municipal Museum. The start and finish are on the athletics track at the Čelákovice Municipal Stadium. Registration is online, and the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Olympijský běh - Červená Lhota
description: The Olympic Run in Červená Lhota is a traditional race that starts by the fairytale-like Červená Lhota Castle. Runners follow the blue hiking trail through the villages of Samosoly and Pohoří and across the dam of Kardaš Pond, mostly along field and forest paths. The race is ceremonially started with a shot from a historic weapon, and by taking part you support the Czech Olympic Foundation. The race is for adults over 15 and offers a pleasant sporting atmosphere, with refreshments provided by volunteer firefighters.

name: Olympijský běh - Červené Pečky
description: The Olympic Run in Červené Pečky is a new location in the Kolín area, offering a course suitable for beginners too. The adult main race is 4.5 km long and runs 90% over easy terrain around the football pitch and a small local wood, with the remaining 10% on asphalt. Shorter courses adapted to children’s age and ability are available. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation; part of the entry fee goes towards supporting children’s participation in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Česká Lípa
description: The Olympic Run in Česká Lípa is a newcomer to the running calendar, centered around the renovated U Ploučnice municipal stadium. Runners set off toward Holý vrch, the city’s western landmark, then return along the Ploučnice River to the stadium, where the start and finish are located. The event is open to adults and children, with several shorter-distance children’s races. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Česká Skalice
description: The Olympic Run in Česká Skalice is part of the nationwide Olympic Day event, which celebrates sport and Olympic values such as friendship, fair play, and respect. The race offers routes for adults and children, and every participant contributes part of their entry fee to support children’s sports. The event is open to everyone, regardless of ability, and is an ideal opportunity to enjoy being active together in the beautiful Hradec Králové Region. The Olympic Run brings people and sports together for a day full of sporting activities and Olympic spirit.

name: Olympijský běh - České Budějovice
description: The Olympic Run in České Budějovice is a traditional race for fans of challenging terrain. The 7 km route crosses the U Špačků ford, follows the right bank of the Malše River to Roudné, and returns to the boathouse. The race is open to adults and children, with a separate 1.5 km route for the children’s races. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00 by the Hanace boathouse in České Budějovice.

name: Olympijský běh - Dačice
description: The Olympic Run in Dačice is a traditional sporting event held in the beautiful grounds of the Dačice State Chateau park. The race follows a route mainly along forest and field paths, suitable for adults and children. The event also features an accompanying program, with the option to visit the chateau and the town museum. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation, which encourages children to take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Děčín
description: The Olympic Run in Děčín is a traditional regional race held at the confluence of the Elbe and Ploučnice rivers. The start and finish are located in front of the Kajak Děčín boathouse. The 4.6 km main race route follows a cycle path almost through the city centre, with asphalt and paved surfaces. The event also includes children’s races over distances from 200 to 1,000 metres. Participants can enjoy the beautiful surroundings, with views of Děčín Castle, the Elbe Canyon and lookout towers, while also supporting the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Dřevěnice
description: The Olympic Run in Dřevěnice is a traditional regional running race with a course of approximately five kilometres. It starts with a challenging climb into the forest above the Dolánky part of the municipality, then heads to a pond, where the route continues on flat asphalt roads, crossing the main road. The finish is at the volleyball courts, which offer full facilities. The race is suitable for adults and children, with shorter children’s races ranging from 50 to 1,200 metres. The race starts at 18:00, and registration is available online only.

name: Olympijský běh - Háj ve Slezsku
description: The Olympic Run in Háj ve Slezsku is part of the nationwide Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values. The event offers courses for adults and children, including a shorter 4 km and a longer 8 km course for adults, as well as children’s races ranging from 60 to 1,000 metres. The start is at the school sports grounds of ZŠ Háj ve Slezsku, and the event has a welcoming atmosphere, with the opportunity to donate to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online, and the event is suitable for the general public, who can enjoy a route through the village and around the athletics track.

name: Olympijský běh - Havířov
description: The Olympic Run in Havířov is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place in the Moravian-Silesian Region and offers a 5 km course. The main category starts at 18:00 at Nealko bar Na Vyhlídce in Havířov. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate a day of sport by running.

name: Olympijský běh - Hluboké Mašůvky
description: The Olympic Run in Hluboké Mašůvky is part of the nationwide Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values such as friendship, fair play and respect. The event offers a 5 km adult race and children’s races of 100, 200 and 300 metres. The start is at the football pitch in Hluboké Mašůvky. The main race begins at 18:00 and is started live on Český rozhlas. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. Toilets, a changing room, a baggage storage area and showers are available, and children can enjoy a bouncy castle.

name: Olympijský běh - Holešov
description: The Olympic Run in Holešov is the country’s largest running event, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place in the beautiful setting of the château gardens in Holešov and offers a mixed 5 km race. The main category starts at 18:00, making it an enjoyable evening run for the general public and athletes alike. The event is part of the broader running movement of the Czech Athletics Federation, which promotes running and a healthy lifestyle.

name: Olympijský běh - Holetín
description: The Olympic Run in Holetín returns after a break with a varied course along roads, paved paths, meadows and country trails. The race is open to adults and children, and by taking part you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The start and registration take place at the Holetín swimming pool complex, which also has basic facilities. The race starts at 18:00 with a live broadcast from Czech Radio, and online registration is available.

name: Olympijský běh - Horní Jelení
description: The Olympic Run in Horní Jelení is a traditional running race with a beautiful route through the local forest and around Pětinoha Pond. It offers races for adults and children, including a 6 km race for adults and shorter 2.5 km and 500 m races for children in different age categories. The race takes place at Komenského Square and starts at 18:00. The atmosphere is friendly, and the event supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online, and the race is timed using chip timing.

name: Olympijský běh - Horoměřice
description: The Olympic Run in Horoměřice offers a 7 km running course completed in two laps. The route is mostly dirt and gravel, with sections of paving stones and concrete slabs. Two-thirds of each lap run gently downhill, while the final third challenges runners with an uphill stretch. Horoměřice is hosting the Olympic Run for the sixth time, and part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The race is suitable for adults and children, with shorter 500 m and 1,000 m races for children.

name: Olympijský běh - Hradec Králové
description: The Olympic Run in Hradec Králové is the largest running event in the Czech Republic, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the country. The race starts at 18:00 near Štefánikova Elementary School and features a 5 km course. The event is open to the general public and runners of all abilities who want to celebrate the day of sport with a run. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Hudčice
description: The Olympic Run in Hudčice is a traditional regional race held on a loop around the village, along asphalt and dirt roads, including a climb to the quarries above the village. The event also includes children’s races of 200 and 700 metres. It is open to all age groups and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only.

name: Olympijský běh - Chlumec nad Cidlinou
description: The Olympic Run in Chlumec nad Cidlinou is a traditional regional race held on the athletics track by Slavíček Hall. The route follows paved and dirt roads, starting and finishing at the stadium. The race is part of the Olympic Day celebrations, and participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation’s work promoting children’s participation in sport. Alongside the main race for adults, there is also a children’s race, making it possible for the whole family and sports enthusiasts of all ages to take part.

name: Olympijský běh - Chomutov
description: The Olympic Run in Chomutov takes place in the picturesque Bezruč Valley, where the pleasant climate and shade provide ideal conditions for achieving great results. The race features out-and-back road routes with a gentle climb to the turnarounds, rewarding runners in the second half of the race. Both shorter and longer routes are available: 10 km and 5 km, respectively. The event is suitable for the general public and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Chotiměř
description: The Olympic Run in Chotiměř is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race features a mixed-terrain 6 km course starting by the municipal office in Chotiměř. The main category starts at 18:00. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate the day of sport by running.

name: Olympijský běh - Ivančice
description: The Olympic Run in Ivančice is part of a nationwide celebration of Olympic Day, bringing together athletes of all ages. The adult race runs mostly on sandy terrain along the Jihlava and Rokytná rivers, with natural landmarks at U Šneka and U Dvou bobrů. Children’s races take place on the athletics track, which is also the start and finish venue for the adult races. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. The main race starts at 18:00 at the Ivančice Municipal Stadium.

name: Olympijský běh - Jihlava
location: Letní kino athletic oval, Jihlava, Vysočina, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Jihlava traditionally takes place at the summer cinema venue and athletics track, offering a family-friendly atmosphere full of support and the joy of movement. The race is open to all age groups, with courses for adults and children on mixed terrain. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation, which helps children take part in sports. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is part of the wider Olympic Day, celebrating sport and Olympic values.

name: Olympijský běh - Kamenice
description: The Olympic Run in Kamenice is a traditional regional race that has been held since 2016 in the picturesque Vysočina region. The race offers moderately challenging courses on unpaved roads and asphalt around three Kamenice ponds, with a choice of a shorter 2.5 km loop or a longer 5 km loop. Special courses of varying lengths are available for children, according to age category. Participants support the Czech Olympic Foundation through their entry fees, helping to promote children’s participation in sport. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only.

name: Olympijský běh - Karviná
description: The Olympic Run in Karviná is a traditional race starting in the historic T. G. Masaryk Square in Karviná-Fryštát. The route passes the Larisch family chateau and through the chateau park, then heads to the city’s landmark, the Darkov Bridge, before returning via the Spa Park to the finish. The race is open to adults and children up to 15 years old, with shorter courses for the children’s races. The event supports the Czech Olympic Foundation and offers a friendly atmosphere, an accompanying programme, and the opportunity for athletes with disabilities to participate in wheelchairs (handbikes).

name: Olympijský běh - Klášterec nad Orlicí
description: The Olympic Run in Klášterec nad Orlicí is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place on the asphalt court by the Sokol Hall and offers 10 km and 5 km courses. The main category starts at 18:00, and the race is suitable for the general public as well as athletes. It is organized by a team of organizers in cooperation with the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Kolín
description: The Olympic Run in Kolín is a traditional sporting event being held for the fourth time as part of the Czech Olympic Committee’s nationwide Olympic Day event. The races take place in the picturesque Borky Forest Park, with two routes: 3 km for adults and 1 km for children. The routes follow forest paths and a cycle path along the Elbe, offering beautiful views and a pleasant running surface. There’s a bouncy castle for children and a photo booth for all participants. The atmosphere is full of sporting spirit and camaraderie. The start and finish are by the bears in Borky Forest Park.

name: Olympijský běh - Kralice nad Oslavou
description: The Olympic Run in Kralice nad Oslavou is a regional running race on a 4 km route along a dirt road and partly on an asphalt road. The race is open to adults and children, with children’s races ranging from 250 to 800 metres. The start is by the football pitch, and the main race begins at 18:00, announced on air by Czech Radio. Participants’ entry fees go to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online only; it will not be possible to register at the venue.

name: Olympijský běh - Krymlov
description: The Olympic Run in Krymlov is a traditional regional race held to celebrate Olympic Day. The event offers a 6.5 km course for adults, as well as children’s races of 200 m and 800 m. The start and registration are in the center of the village by Krymlovská hospoda, where refreshments are available before and after the race. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation, supporting sports development.

name: Olympijský běh - Liberec
description: The Olympic Run in Liberec is a traditional sporting event held at the Sport Park Liberec complex on the inline skating track around the athletics stadium. It offers races for children and adults, with distances from 150 metres up to 6 km, suitable for the general public, including wheelchair users and handbike riders. The main race starts at 18:00. Registration is online only, with the option to register multiple runners at once. The programme also includes a group warm-up and facilities with toilets, changing rooms, showers and a baggage storage area. The entry fee supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Líbeznice
description: The Olympic Run in Líbeznice is a new addition to this traditional sporting event, which brings together runners of all ages. The races take place at Areál zdraví, which offers modern sports facilities in the peaceful, leafy surroundings of the village, known for its interesting architectural features. The routes follow asphalt, paved and unpaved paths through the village and surrounding area, including the Mratínka trail, which was created from a former railway spur. The event is not only a sporting occasion but also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation and enjoy a friendly atmosphere and the joy of movement.

name: Olympijský běh - Lovosice
description: The Olympic Run in Lovosice is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place at the athletics stadium in Lovosice and offers 8 km and 4 km courses. The main category starts at 18:00, and the race is open to runners of all abilities and sports enthusiasts. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Mělník
description: The Olympic Run in Mělník is a traditional race held amid the picturesque natural surroundings of the Elbe Lowlands, near the Elbe River and Na Polabí Park. The children’s races take place on an unpaved surface in the park, while adults run along a paved asphalt cycle path with no elevation gain. The event is suitable for the general public and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only.

name: Olympijský běh - Město Touškov
description: The Olympic Run in Město Touškov is a traditional regional race that passes through the town’s historic centre, by the Baroque Church of St. John the Baptist and the Touškov pond. The course combines grass and asphalt surfaces and offers an enjoyable run through picturesque surroundings. The race is open to adults and children, with several course distances, and also supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The start and registration are at the TJ Sokol sports complex. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio.

name: Olympijský běh - Most
description: The Olympic Run in Most takes place in the Matylda recreation area and offers two routes for adults—a shorter 4 km and a longer 8 km course—along the paved inline skating path around Lake Matylda. The race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Český rozhlas radio. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online only until June 6; registration will not be available on site. Showers, toilets, a changing room and a baggage storage facility are available for runners. Parking is available in the Matylda area.

name: Olympijský běh - Olomouc
organizer: Český olympijský výbor a Klub vytrvalostních sportů Olomouc
description: The Olympic Run in Olomouc is part of the T-Mobile Olympic Run and offers a bronze-level race with a charitable dimension. The event takes place in Olomouc-Hejčín and includes a 5 km adult race and free children’s races for children up to 15 years old. The race starts at 6 p.m., with the start broadcast on Czech Radio. The entry fee includes a race pack with a sports bag and gifts from partners, and part of the fee goes to support the Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Opava Suché Lazce
description: The Olympic Run in Opava-Suché Lazce is the country’s largest running event, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race covers a 5 km course and is open to the general public and sports enthusiasts alike. It starts at the municipal football pitch at 18:00, and the event has a friendly, motivating atmosphere for all runners. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletic Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrava Hošťálkovice
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrava-Hošťálkovice is a traditional running race on paved paths over rolling terrain. It offers two routes for adults—a longer 10 km route and a shorter 5 km route—with the start at the sports complex by ZŠ Výhledy-Hošťálkovice. Children may also take part with permission from a legal guardian, and the event contributes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio. Toilets, changing rooms, showers, and parking are available by MŠ Výhledy.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrava Komenského sady
location: Komenského sady, Ostrava, Moravian-Silesian Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrava’s Komenský Gardens is a traditional sporting event held in a beautiful park along the Ostravice River. The race offers routes for adults and children. The main race starts at 18:00 and is broadcast on Czech Radio. By taking part, participants contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. Registration is online, and the race is suitable for the general public, including wheelchair users and handbikes.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrov u Karlových Varů
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrov near Karlovy Vary is part of Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values. The race takes place in the pleasant surroundings of the castle park and follows a sandy path. Participants can run the 5 km course. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is suitable for the general public, including children accompanied by an adult.

name: Olympijský běh - Palkovice
description: The Olympic Run in Palkovice is a traditional regional race held in beautiful surroundings, with a combination of paved roads, forest paths and terrain. The adult course is approximately 5,100 metres long and includes a hill, adding interest and challenge to the race. Children can take part in races over 200 m, 400 m and 1,600 m, making it an event for the whole family. The event is also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation and enjoy a sporting atmosphere in the community. The start and registration are behind the gym in Palkovice; the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Olympijský běh - Pardubice
description: The Olympic Run in Pardubice is a traditional race held in the Studánka forest park. The 3.8 km course runs mainly along forest paths with some asphalt sections and is suitable for beginners thanks to its mostly flat terrain with a few climbs. The event also includes 1.1 km children’s races. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation, and can choose to register with or without a T-shirt.

name: Olympijský běh - Pelhřimov
description: The Olympic Run in Pelhřimov is a traditional running race held in a picturesque town on the edge of the Bohemian-Moravian Highlands. The race offers courses for children and adults, including a longer 7.2 km route and a shorter 4.8 km route, which run through the town parks and surrounding area. The start is at the Senior Citizens’ Home on Radětínská Street, and the race supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. Online registration is available, with the option to sign up multiple runners at once. Pelhřimov is also known for its historic landmarks and Festival of Records and Curiosities, giving the race a unique atmosphere.

name: Olympijský běh - Praha Královka
description: The Olympic Run in Prague–Královka is part of a nationwide celebration of Olympic Day, bringing together sports enthusiasts of all ages. The race offers adult runners a challenging 3.8 km course that runs mostly on paved park paths, with some sections off the pavement, including stairs and uneven terrain. Shorter distances of 350 m, 550 m and 1,100 m are available for children. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children with limited financial means in pursuing sports. The main race starts at 18:00. Registration is online only.

name: Olympijský běh - Praha Satalice
description: The Olympic Run in Prague-Satalice is a 5 km race that runs mainly along forest trails in the Satalice Game Reserve, a chestnut-lined avenue, and gravel paths in the forest park. The route is flat and offers runners a pleasant setting, with views over fields and a course that passes the Chapel of St. Anne. A warm-up is provided before the start, and motivational announcements are made during the race. After the race, refreshments, showers, changing rooms, and a bag storage area are available, all in a friendly atmosphere. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Rožnov pod Radhoštěm
description: The Olympic Run in Rožnov pod Radhoštěm is part of the largest running event in the Czech Republic, which is being held for the 40th year. On race day, June 17, sports enthusiasts of all ages can enjoy running and other physical activities. The event is also open to sports clubs and associations, which can organize their own Olympic Day. Registration is available only online on the official website until June 5, with the best entry fee for adults available until the end of March.

name: Olympijský běh - Rychnov nad Kněžnou
description: The Olympic Run in Rychnov nad Kněžnou is returning to the running calendar after a long break and invites all runners to celebrate Olympic Day through movement. The main adult race is 5 km long and starts at the swimming pool complex in Včelné. Children can take part in races from 200 m to 1,500 m, depending on their age category. The event also offers an accompanying program, the chance to try SPARTAN obstacles, and facilities including a bag drop, toilets, and showers. Registration is online, with the option to sign up multiple runners at once, and the entry fee contributes to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Strakonice
description: The Olympic Run in Strakonice is a traditional sporting event being held for the third time at the Podskalí campsite. The race offers routes for adults and children, with adults running 4 km on a mix of natural and paved paths. Children can take part in races of 350 m and 1.2 km, accompanied by an Olympic-themed programme. The main race starts at 18:00, and part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The event is suitable for all age groups and promotes the joy of movement and a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Stříbro
description: The Olympic Run in Stříbro is a traditional running race that takes place mostly along forest paths and supports Olympic ideals and the Czech Olympic Foundation. The program includes a 5 km race for adults and children’s races of 600 and 1,000 metres. The event is held at the TJ Baník Stříbro stadium and offers a pleasant sporting environment, with online registration available. The main race starts at 18:00. Participants have access to changing rooms, toilets, showers and storage. The race is also open to athletes with disabilities using wheelchairs (handbikes).

name: Olympijský běh - Tachov
description: The Olympic Run in Tachov gives runners the chance to take on a mixed course combining natural and asphalt sections along the Mže River. The race is open to both children aged 15 and under and adults, with a capacity of 100 adult and 100 child participants. The start and registration are at the Tachov Sports Complex – Rychta. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio. Registration is online only until June 7; on-site registration will not be available. By purchasing an entry, you contribute CZK 20 to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Tlučeň
description: The Olympic Run in Tlučeň offers a race along a forest trail through the Bohemian Central Highlands, around Plešivec, with approximately 180 metres of elevation gain—one of the highest elevation gains among Olympic Run races. The route is shaded and open to adults and children, with shorter distances for the children’s races. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and the accompanying programme includes, for example, an aikido demonstration. Registration is online; it will not be possible to register on site.

name: Olympijský běh - Trutnov
description: After last year’s debut, the Olympic Run in Trutnov returns for its second edition. The race offers a 5 km route with mixed terrain, starting at the athletics stadium and passing the swimming pool before following forest paths along the Poříčský Ridge, with the finish back at the stadium. Children’s races of 100 to 800 metres will take place in the stadium grounds. The event is not only a sporting challenge but also an opportunity to support a good cause, as part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Tuhaň
description: The Olympic Run in Tuhan is a traditional race held in the beautiful Kokořínsko Protected Landscape Area. The route runs mainly through forests and meadows, with part of it on an asphalt road, offering a pleasant running experience in nature. The event also includes children’s races on the football pitch, making it suitable for the whole family. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Ústí nad Labem
description: The Olympic Run in Ústí nad Labem is a traditional running race held in the beautiful surroundings of Lake Milada. The race offers routes for adults and children, with a choice of shorter or longer routes for adults. The start is near the car park above Lake Milada’s main beach, and the route follows the water before climbing gently to the finish. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation to support children’s participation in sport. The race is suitable for the general public who want to enjoy being active and support a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Valašské Klobouky
description: The Olympic Run in Valašské Klobouky is a traditional sporting event held in the beautiful, hilly landscape of the White Carpathians. The race offers two main routes for adults—a 5-kilometre and a 10-kilometre course—run mostly on asphalt. Children’s races are also held in the enclosed area of the football pitch. The start is at the TJ Spartak Valašské Klobouky football pitch, and participants make a donation to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Vnorovy
description: The Olympic Run in Vnorovy is a traditional regional race on a 6.5 km course along local roads, field tracks and forest paths. Part of the route runs between the Morava River and the Baťa Canal, including a crossing over the Baťa Canal lock. The start and finish are on the athletics track at the Vnorovy sports complex. The race is open to adults and children, with shorter children’s races ranging from 100 to 1,000 metres. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Lelekovice
description: The Olympic Run in Lelekovice is a traditional race held on Olympic Day. Its routes run mostly along field and forest trails, with gently rolling terrain and a steep climb before the finish. The main race is 5 km long and suitable for adults and children, while the children’s races cover shorter distances from 150 to 1,060 metres. After the race, prizes are awarded not only to the winners but also to runners selected in a draw and older participants. The event is followed by a get-together around a fire with music and the option to roast food. Registration is online, and the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Komořany – Čihadlo
description: Komořany - Čihadlo is a 4.88 km running race with 175 metres of elevation gain, held entirely on forest and field paths. The finish is at the summit of Čihadlo. The race is part of the Hill Running Series in Prague and the surrounding area, offering runners an enjoyable experience in a natural setting on a more challenging course.

name: Běh okolo Špilberku
description: The Run Around Špilberk is a traditional running race in Brno, featuring an interesting course around Špilberk Castle. The race is open to men, women, and children of all ages and takes place in the pleasant early evening. Men run five 1.3 km laps, women run three laps, and the lap length for children is adjusted according to age. Refreshments and a baggage drop-off are available after the race. The affordable entry fee is 150 CZK, and registration takes place at the venue before the race.

name: Radimovický koňák
description: Radimovický koňák is a traditional cross-country race held in the village of Radimovice u Želče, attracting runners of all ages every year. The race takes place in the pleasant surroundings of South Bohemia and offers everyone from the youngest children to adult men, who make up the largest category, the chance to test their strength. The event has a long-standing tradition and is a popular sporting occasion in the region.

name: Challenge Gdańsk 2026
description: Challenge Gdańsk to triathlon rozgrywany w pięknej lokalizacji nad Morzem Bałtyckim, w mieście wolności i Solidarności. Zawody obejmują dystans T100, który składa się z 2 km pływania w Zatoce Gdańskiej, 80 km szybkiej trasy rowerowej po Żuławach Wiślanych oraz 18 km biegu wzdłuż gdańskiej plaży i parku Ronalda Reagana. Meta znajduje się na gdańskim molo w Brzeźnie, co zapewnia wyjątkowe wrażenia z finiszu. Impreza jest oficjalnym wyścigiem kwalifikującym i przyciąga zawodników z różnych kategorii, w tym Challenge Women by Brooks.
course_highlights: 2 km pływanie w Zatoce Gdańskiej z startem i metą na plaży Gdańsk Brzeźno
80 km szybka trasa rowerowa po Żuławach Wiślanych przez Kiezmark, Cedry Małe i Koszwały
18 km bieg w 4 pętlach wzdłuż gdańskiej plaży i parku Ronalda Reagana z bufetami na trasie
additional: Start dystansu Sprint o 8:00 z plaży Gdańsk Brzeźno. Biuro zawodów czynne od 10:00 do 20:00. Możliwość wykupienia opcji zwrotu opłaty startowej w przypadku rezygnacji do 31 maja 2027. Trasa rowerowa to dwie szybkie pętle po Żuławach Wiślanych. Trasa biegowa to 4 pętle po 4,5 km z bufetami na każdej pętli. Meta na molo w Gdańsku Brzeźnie. Zawodnicy muszą odebrać pakiet startowy i wziąć udział w odprawie. Organizator zastrzega prawo do zmiany trasy i formuły w przypadku złych warunków atmosferycznych.

name: Nocny Bieg Firmowy Warszawa
description: Nocny Bieg Firmowy w Warszawie to charytatywna sztafeta 5-osobowych drużyn firmowych, która odbędzie się na Torze Służewiec. Każdy uczestnik pokonuje około 5 km po zmroku, a łączny czas drużyny decyduje o wyniku. To wyjątkowa okazja, by spędzić wieczór w integrującej, nocnej atmosferze, wspierając jednocześnie dzieci z Fundacji Everest. Wydarzenie łączy sport, zabawę i pomoc społeczną, tworząc niezapomniane przeżycie dla uczestników.

name: 17 Legionowska Dycha
description: 17. Legionowska Dycha to coroczny bieg na dystansie 10 km, który odbędzie się w Legionowie. Start i meta zlokalizowane są pod Areną Legionowo. Trasa posiada atest PZLA i jest przeznaczona dla dorosłych oraz osób powyżej 16 roku życia, które spełnią wymogi regulaminowe. Wydarzenie obejmuje także bieg towarzyszący „Mundurowa Dziesiątka” dla służb mundurowych i pasjonatów. Uczestnicy mogą liczyć na elektroniczny pomiar czasu oraz limit czasu na pokonanie trasy wynoszący 1 godzinę i 40 minut.

name: Nocny Bieg Świętojański
description: Nocny Bieg Świętojański to coroczna impreza biegowa organizowana w Gdyni, będąca częścią Grand Prix Gdyni 2026. Główny bieg na dystansie 10 km odbywa się w malowniczej scenerii miasta, a towarzyszą mu biegi dziecięce i młodzieżowe. Wydarzenie przyciąga biegaczy z różnych grup wiekowych, oferując sportową rywalizację i integrację w nocnej atmosferze. Organizatorzy zapewniają profesjonalną obsługę oraz dokumentację fotograficzną i wideo z imprezy.

name: Stacjonarne DaVita Run Kraków
description: Stacjonarne DaVita Run Kraków 2026 to charytatywny bieg organizowany w Krakowie, który promuje zdrowy i aktywny styl życia oraz integrację środowiska nefrologów, pacjentów i sympatyków biegania. Uczestnicy mogą wybrać dystans 2,5 km lub 5 km, a czas na ukończenie biegu wynosi 60 minut. Opłata startowa w całości przekazywana jest na rzecz Ogólnopolskiego Stowarzyszenia Moje Nerki, a każdy uczestnik otrzymuje koszulkę z oryginalną grafiką imprezy. Dla osób, które nie mogą uczestniczyć osobiście, dostępna jest także opcja biegu wirtualnego.

name: 44. Heiligenröder Abendlauf
price_range: modest registration fees, free for Bambinis
description: The 44th Heiligenröder Evening Run is a traditional night road race in Niestetal, Germany, and part of the Nordhessencup running series. The event offers distances for all ages and ability levels, from 400 m for Bambinis to 20.35 km for experienced runners. It combines competitive racing with more casual running options: Bambinis, walkers, and Nordic walkers are timed but not ranked. Bambinis can take part for free, while children, teenagers, and adults pay moderate entry fees.
course_highlights: Night road race in Niestetal-Heiligenrode
Distances from 400 m to 20.35 km
Part of the Nordhessencup running series
additional: Bambinis run for free; entry fees for children, teenagers, and adults are moderate. The event is listed on laufen.de. Typical June weather: approx. 23 °C, mostly sunny. Night race, multiple distances, events for all ages, part of the Nordhessencup running series.

name: 21. Laatzen Leinelauf
description: The 21st Laatzen Leinelauf is taking place, offering runners routes of 3.5 km, 6.5 km, and 10 km through the idyllic Leine floodplain, with nature, water, and wide-open meadows. The event also includes a 1.2 km Bambini run and a 6.5 km walking category. The 10 km route includes a team classification for mixed teams. The traditional Laatzen Wine Festival takes place alongside the race, rounding off the evening with culinary and musical highlights.

name: 40. Braunschweiger Nachtlauf
description: The 40th Braunschweig Night Run offers a wide range of sporting events for all age groups, from Bambini races to recreational runs. The races pass through Braunschweig city center, with the start and finish on Bohlweg; the Bambini races start at Burgplatz. The event is known for its special atmosphere and for the support of the Braunschweigische Sparkassenstiftung, which makes the event possible and helps it grow. The race bib serves as a ticket for public transport in Braunschweig on the day of the event. All finishers can download certificates, and baggage drop-off is open until 23:30.

name: SportScheck RUN Hamburg
description: The SportScheck RUN Hamburg is a traditional night run around the Outer Alster, held in a lively evening atmosphere. Depending on the distance, runners can complete one or two laps of the 7.5 km route around the Alster. There are special 1 km and 1.8 km races for children. The start and finish area in Alsterpark offers a special atmosphere, with a cheering zone, photo point and a large medal wall bringing the Hanseatic flair to life at dusk.

name: Brunsbüttler Citylauf
description: The Brunsbüttel City Run is an urban running event in Brunsbüttel, Schleswig-Holstein, featuring 5 km and 10 km races, as well as a short stadium run for children. The start and finish are at the Bildungszentrum stadium on Ziegelweg. The event is open to adults, young people, school groups, corporate teams, and children—not just club athletes. The 5 km course is a loop, while the 10 km course is run twice. The youngest participants can take part in an approximately 400 m children’s run in the stadium, making it easy for families to follow all the action.

name: Högl-Berglauf
description: The Högl Mountain Run is a long-standing event held annually in Ainring since 1980. The course covers 9.8 km with 480 metres of elevation gain and finishes above the Neubichler Alm. In 2004, the German Mountain Running Championships were held on the extended course. Alongside the main race, the Schüler-Gipfel-Sprint is a regular part of the programme and offers young runners an exciting challenge.

name: Jemgumer Dörploop
description: The Jemgumer Dörploop is a varied running event in Jemgum, offering different distances for all age groups. The course consists of 5.3 km laps, which are run multiple times depending on the event. In addition to individual races, there is also a relay race with four runners. The event features electronic timing using reusable transponders and offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with certificates, medals, and prizes for participants.
course_highlights: 5.3 km loop course
Relay race with 4 × 5.3 km laps
Water stations along the course and refreshments at the finish
additional: Late entries are possible up to 60 minutes before the respective start, with a late-entry fee of €3.00 for all events except the Bambini and schoolchildren’s races. Timing is electronic, using reusable transponders worn on the foot, which must be returned after the race (€10.00 fee if not returned). Drinks and fruit from EDEKA Blank are available at the finish.

name: Lippe-Sommer-Serie 2025 Lauf 2: 34. Wöbbeler Volkslauf "Rund um den Hahnenberg"
description: The course runs around Hahnenberg and offers runners a varied challenge. The event is suitable for runners of all ages and promises a pleasant atmosphere in typical June weather, usually with sunny conditions.

name: Krakonosova stovka
description: Krakonošova stovka is a traditional long-distance hike with a history dating back to 1966. The 100 km route crosses the challenging mountain terrain of the Krkonoše Mountains, with over 3,000 metres of elevation gain. It starts and finishes in Vrchlabí and passes notable places such as Špindlerův Mlýn, Sněžka and Pec pod Sněžkou. In addition to the main K100 route, shorter options are available: K50, K25 and the B25 running route. The event is for endurance hikers and runners who want to experience the beauty of the Krkonoše Mountains within a challenging 24-hour time limit.
course_highlights: Challenging mountain terrain with over 3,000 m of elevation gain
The route passes through Špindlerův Mlýn, Sněžka and Pec pod Sněžkou
Start and finish in Vrchlabí
additional: UMARA isotonic drinks are available at selected checkpoints. UMARA sports nutrition can be purchased before the start. Parking is limited due to a road closure; participants are advised to use the designated car parks and not obstruct traffic. According to the official website, registration for the 2027 edition is expected to open on 1 February 2027. Information on the price, time limit and refreshments available for K100 applies to the 2026 edition.

name: Běh metropole MČ Praha 14 - Večerní běh
description: The Běh metropole MČ Praha 14 - Evening Run is part of the BĚH METROPOLE series of public running races, which promotes a healthy lifestyle and a sense of belonging among Prague residents to their city district. The race takes place in Kejřův Park and offers a pleasant evening-running atmosphere, with the opportunity to represent your district. The start is scheduled for the evening, adding to the unique experience of running in an urban setting. The organizers emphasize competition and community spirit among participants of all ages.

name: Okolo Rudného
description: Okolo Rudného is a running race in the Vysočina region offering two distances: 8.2 km for men and 4.2 km for women. The route follows unpaved forest roads and trails, providing a pleasant running experience in nature. The race is part of the Běžec Vysočiny Cup and is suitable for runners looking for a trail run with a gentle profile. Okolo Rudného is a traditional race that attracts runners from the region and surrounding areas.

name: 54 Memoriał Żylewicza - Bieg Amatorów
description: 54. Memoriał Józefa Żylewicza to prestiżowy mityng lekkoatletyczny organizowany corocznie od 1973 roku przez Klub Lekkoatletyczny LECHIA Gdańsk. Wydarzenie upamiętnia wybitnego trenera i działacza sportowego, Józefa Żylewicza, jednego z twórców KS LECHIA Gdańsk oraz współtwórcę sukcesów polskiej reprezentacji lekkoatletycznej. Memoriał odbywa się na Stadionie Lekkoatletyki i Rugby w Gdańsku i łączy profesjonalizm sportowy z otwartością dla lokalnej społeczności, przyciągając zawodników z Polski i zagranicy. W ramach Memoriału organizowany jest także Amatorski Bieg na 3000 m „Szybka Strzała Północy”, otwarty dla wszystkich miłośników biegania, bez limitów wiekowych i wymagań sportowych.

name: Drabina Wałbrzyska
description: Drabina Wałbrzyska to wymagająca kondycyjnie trasa górska w Sudetach, przebiegająca przez Góry Wałbrzyskie i Kamienne. Na dystansie około 78 km uczestnicy pokonują niemal 4 tysiące metrów przewyższenia, zdobywając ponad 30 szczytów. Trasa tworzy pętlę, start i meta mogą być z każdego punktu na trasie. Jest to doskonała propozycja dla osób chcących poznać walory krajobrazowe i przyrodnicze tej części Sudetów, oferująca ambitne wyzwanie bez konieczności wyjazdu w wysokie góry.

name: I Nocny Półmaraton Piaseczyńśki
description: Nocny Półmaraton Piaseczyński to wyjątkowy bieg uliczny na dystansie 21,0975 km, który odbywa się nocą przez malownicze i oświetlone ulice Piaseczna oraz okoliczne miejscowości. Trasa jest certyfikowana przez PZLA, płaska i szybka, idealna dla osób chcących poprawić swoje rekordy życiowe. Uczestnicy mogą liczyć na profesjonalną organizację, pełne zabezpieczenie medyczne oraz bogate punkty odżywcze. Po biegu każdy finisher otrzymuje okolicznościowy medal, a na mecie czeka strefa regeneracyjna z napojami i posiłkiem. Impreza to także niezapomniana atmosfera nocnego biegu pod gwiazdami, wspierana przez liczne atrakcje i konkursy dla kibiców.
course_highlights: Certyfikowana trasa PZLA o długości 21,0975 km
Płaska, szybka trasa z minimalnymi różnicami wysokości
Trasa przebiega przez Piaseczno, Górki Szymona, Głosków i Jazgarzew
additional: Pakiety startowe odbierane są w dniach 15 - 19 czerwca w Decathlon Piaseczno oraz 20 czerwca w Biurze Zawodów. Limit uczestników półmaratonu to 2000 osób. Limit czasu na pokonanie półmaratonu to 3 godziny brutto, z limitem 1,5 godziny na półmetku. Na trasie znajdują się trzy punkty odżywcze (ok. 5., 10. i 15. km). Po biegu dostępna jest strefa finish z wodą, izotonikami, posiłkiem regeneracyjnym, muzyką i ekranem LED. Organizowany jest konkurs na najlepszą strefę kibica. Możliwość cesji pakietu do 31.05.2027 za opłatą 20 zł. Koszulka okolicznościowa dostępna osobno za 75 zł (zamówienia do 29.05.2027).

name: XII BIEG WIERCHAMI

late_fee.price: wg stawki obowiązującej w dniu dokonania wpłaty
wg stawki obowiązującej w dniu dokonania wpłaty

description: Bieg Wierchami to górskie wyzwanie odbywające się w Beskidzie Sądeckim, oferujące różnorodne dystanse od 11 km do 100 km. Trasy prowadzą przez malownicze szlaki z dużymi przewyższeniami, zapewniając biegaczom kontakt z naturą i wymagające podbiegi. Impreza organizowana jest przez Stowarzyszenie Visegrad Maraton w Rytrze, które dba o profesjonalną organizację i bogaty pakiet startowy. Starty odbywają się w Ośrodku RyterSKI, a uczestnicy mogą liczyć na punkty odżywcze i piękne krajobrazy.
course_highlights: Corno Owca 11 km z przewyższeniem około +394 m/-393 m
Waligóra 30 km z przewyższeniem około +1124 m/-1124 m, w tym podbieg pod Wielki Rogacz i najwyższy punkt trasy Radziejowa
Trasy prowadzą przez Beskid Sądecki, mijając charakterystyczne punkty jak wiatrak i ryterski bunkier
additional: Pakiet startowy zapewniany dla osób zapisanych i opłaconych przed terminem. Biuro zawodów mieści się w Ośrodku RyterSKI. Trasy posiadają punkty odżywcze, a meta znajduje się przy drodze asfaltowej po mijaniu charakterystycznych punktów jak wiatrak i bunkier.

name: 16. PKO Rybnicki Półmaraton Księżycowy
description: Rybnicki Półmaraton Księżycowy to coroczna impreza biegowa organizowana przez MOSiR Rybnik, która przyciąga biegaczy z różnych regionów. Bieg odbywa się w malowniczym mieście Rybnik, oferując uczestnikom wyjątkową atmosferę i sportowe emocje. Jest to wydarzenie o ugruntowanej tradycji, które promuje aktywny tryb życia i integrację lokalnej społeczności.

name: Mistrzostwa Gminy Kąty Wrocławskie w Biegach Przełajowych. Bieg 4: Kąty Wrocławskie
location: Kąty Wrocławskie, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Polska
description: Mistrzostwa Gminy Kąty Wrocławskie w Biegach Przełajowych to cykl czterech biegów odbywających się na malowniczych trasach w gminie Kąty Wrocławskie. Trasy zachwycają różnorodnością terenu i pięknem przyrody Parku Krajobrazowego Doliny Bystrzycy. Uczestnicy mogą startować w pojedynczych biegach lub w całym cyklu, a po ukończeniu co najmniej trzech biegów klasyfikowani są w generalnej klasyfikacji. Po każdym biegu zawodnicy otrzymują pamiątkowy medal, a po zebraniu wszystkich czterech medali tworzą one spójną całość z motywem konturu granic gminy. Finałowy bieg odbywa się w Kątach Wrocławskich na trasie o długości 5 km.
course_highlights: Trasy przebiegają przez Park Krajobrazowy Doliny Bystrzycy
Różnorodne nawierzchnie i ukształtowanie terenu: pagórki, winnice, lasy
Finałowa trasa 5 km między Kątami Wrocławskimi, Jurczycami i Sośnicą
additional: Możliwość startu w pojedynczych biegach lub całym cyklu. Aby być sklasyfikowanym w klasyfikacji generalnej, należy ukończyć co najmniej 3 z 4 biegów. Kategorie OPEN dla kobiet i mężczyzn oraz klasyfikacje drużynowe (min. 3 zawodników). Uroczyste wręczenie pucharów na zakończenie cyklu.

name: ULTRA TURNICKI
description: Ultra Turnicki to wyjątkowy festiwal biegowy odbywający się w malowniczym regionie Pogórza Przemyskiego i Gór Sanocko-Turczańskich. Zawody oferują zarówno zimowe, jak i letnie biegi na różnych dystansach, łącząc sportową rywalizację z bogatym programem kulturalnym i festiwalowym. Trasy prowadzą przez unikalne krajobrazy, a uczestnicy mogą liczyć na dobrze zaopatrzone punkty odżywcze oraz integrację z lokalną społecznością. Start i meta zlokalizowane są w Huwnikach, co zapewnia łatwy dojazd i atrakcyjne możliwości noclegowe.
course_highlights: Trasy prowadzą przez Pogórze Przemyskie i Góry Sanocko-Turczańskie
Letni bieg odbywa się podczas festiwalu Wianki z warsztatami i koncertami
Zimowy bieg oferuje widoki z przełęczy Żytnego i dwa punkty odżywcze na trasie
additional: Letni bieg oferuje cztery dystanse: 10 km, 24 km, 48 km i 75 km, z transportem na start i bogatym programem festiwalowym. Zimowy bieg ma dwa dystanse: 15 km i 36 km, z transportem na start i punktami odżywczymi na trasie. Po biegach organizowane są integracje, prelekcje i ceremonia wręczenia nagród. Możliwość noclegu w gospodarstwach agroturystycznych oraz rozbicia namiotu w sezonie letnim. Transport publiczny i dojazd autostradą oraz koleją do Huwnik.

name: Wieczorna Piątka
description: Wieczorna Piątka to bieg na dystansie 5000 metrów, który odbywa się na tartanowej bieżni Stadionu Miejskiego w Makowie Mazowieckim. Zawody zaplanowano na godzinę 18:00 i będą podzielone na serie według prognozowanego czasu uczestników. Organizatorem jest Lekkoatletyczny Klub Sportowy Maków Mazowiecki, a limit uczestników wynosi 200 osób. Bieg jest otwarty dla osób powyżej 15 roku życia, z wymaganą pisemną zgodą opiekuna dla niepełnoletnich.
course_highlights: Dystans 5000 m na tartanowej bieżni stadionu
Jedno okrążenie ma 400 m
Podział na serie według prognozowanego czasu biegu
additional: Limit uczestników wynosi 200 pakietów startowych. Opłaty można dokonać online przez platformę Przelewy24 lub przelewem na konto klubu. Szczegółowy program z podziałem na serie zostanie opublikowany na stronie w tygodniu przed zawodami.

name: 15 Górski Półmaraton Pętli Tatrzańskiej
description: Górski Półmaraton Pętli Tatrzańskiej to górski bieg odbywający się w Koszalinie, na trasie wokół Góry Chełmskiej. Uczestnicy mogą wybrać dystans 10,55 km (ćwierćmaraton) lub 21,1 km (półmaraton), który składa się z dwóch pętli. Start i meta znajdują się przy placu Gościńcowym w okolicach szczytu Góry Chełmskiej, a trasa prowadzi przez malownicze tereny leśne z widokami. Bieg organizowany jest przez Stowarzyszenie Sport, rekreacja i wolontariat „SFX” i ma charakter rekreacyjno-sportowy, promując aktywny styl życia i turystykę w lasach.
course_highlights: Trasa górska wokół Góry Chełmskiej z przewyższeniem do 136,2 m n.p.m.
Dwa dystanse do wyboru: 10,55 km (jedna pętla) i 21,1 km (dwie pętle)
Start i meta przy placu Gościńcowym między sanktuarium a wieżą widokową
additional: Biuro zawodów czynne od 9:00 do 10:30. Start honorowy z placu między sanktuarium a wieżą widokową. Wręczenie nagród około 14:30. Trasa jest dobrze oznakowana i zmierzona. Możliwość wyboru dystansu podczas biegu. Darowizny na cele statutowe Stowarzyszenia SFX są podstawą udziału i nie podlegają zwrotowi ani przeniesieniu.

name: 43 Strzeliński Rogaining
location: Kamiennik, Strzelin County, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Polska
description: Strzeliński Rogaining to pieszy rajd na orientację, w którym drużyny 2-5 osobowe planują własną trasę, aby w wyznaczonym czasie odwiedzić jak najwięcej punktów kontrolnych rozmieszczonych w terenie i oznaczonych na mapie. Zawody są otwarte dla uczestników w różnym wieku i o różnym stopniu zaawansowania, zarówno dla pasjonatów, jak i osób startujących rekreacyjnie. Rogaining ma charakter turystyczno-sportowy i jest doskonałą formą aktywności na łonie natury, pozwalającą odpocząć od codzienności. Organizowany przez Polskie Towarzystwo Turystyczno-Krajoznawcze Oddział Ziemi Strzelińskiej, ma wieloletnią tradycję i cieszy się międzynarodowym zainteresowaniem.
course_highlights: Trasa wyznaczana przez drużyny samodzielnie, z możliwością wyboru punktów kontrolnych o różnym stopniu trudności
Punkty kontrolne rozmieszczone w terenie, oznaczone na mapie i w terenie flagami nawigacyjnymi
Dystanse od kilku do kilkudziesięciu kilometrów, z możliwością zmiany trasy w trakcie zawodów
additional: Zespoły poruszają się wyłącznie pieszo, używając mapy i kompasu do orientacji. Zawody są otwarte dla wszystkich, bez względu na wiek i płeć. Można opracować własny wariant trasy o dowolnej długości, od około 5 km do nawet 70 km, i zmieniać go podczas pokonywania trasy. Impreza ma charakter turystyczno-sportowy, odpowiednia także dla rodzin i osób rekreacyjnie uprawiających sport.

name: Bieg Dwie Wieże
description: Bieg Dwie Wieże to bieg na dystansie około 15 km, odbywający się w Kopalinie. Trasa prowadzi drogą gruntową, plażą oraz chodnikiem, oferując różnorodne podłoże i malownicze widoki. Limit czasu na pokonanie trasy wynosi 2,5 godziny, a liczba uczestników jest ograniczona do 250 osób. Zawodnicy otrzymują chip do pomiaru czasu oraz numer startowy, a na trasie dostępne są punkty z wodą oraz na mecie posiłek regeneracyjny. Impreza jest profesjonalnie zabezpieczona medycznie i fotografowana.
course_highlights: Trasa o długości około 15 km
Bieg po drodze gruntowej, plaży i chodniku
Punkty z wodą na 4, 8, 12 km oraz na mecie
additional: Biuro zawodów czynne 19.06 13:00 - 19:00 oraz 20.06 8:00 - 9:45 (zamknięcie weryfikacji o 9:45). Weryfikacja tożsamości obowiązkowa (dowód/legitymacja). Chip do pomiaru czasu jest obowiązkowy, pobierany w biurze i zwracany na mecie. Na mecie dostępna woda i posiłek regeneracyjny. Zabezpieczenie medyczne zapewnione. Udział oznacza akceptację wykorzystania wizerunku. Zawodnicy proszeni są o przestrzeganie zasad porządkowych i przepisów ruchu drogowego.

name: Challenge Poland
description: Challenge Poland to prestiżowy triathlon rozgrywany w Gdańsku, oferujący różnorodne dystanse, w tym popularny dystans T100. Zawody odbywają się nad Morzem Bałtyckim, z szybkim i płaskim odcinkiem rowerowym oraz malowniczą trasą biegową wzdłuż plaży i parku Ronald Reagan. Start i meta znajdują się na pięknym molo w Gdańsku, co stanowi wyjątkową atrakcję dla zawodników i kibiców. Wydarzenie jest oficjalnym kwalifikatorem i cieszy się uznaniem wśród triathlonistów na całym świecie.
course_highlights: 2,0 km pływania na plaży miejskiej przy molo Brzeźno
80 km płaskiej i szybkiej trasy rowerowej przez Żuławy Wiślane
18 km biegu wzdłuż plaży Gdańsk i parku Ronald Reagan z malowniczym finiszem na molo
additional: Możliwość wykupienia opcji anulacji rejestracji do 31 maja 2027. Specjalne zniżki dla drużyn 10+ osób. Trasa rowerowa przebiega m.in. obok stadionu Polsat Plus Arena. Starty odbywają się w kilku kategoriach i dystansach, w tym solo i sztafety. Biuro zawodów i expo zlokalizowane na plaży Brzeźno. Ceremonie dekoracji na molo w Gdańsku.

name: VI Bieg Świętojański
description: VI Bieg Świętojański to bieg na dystansie 10 km odbywający się w malowniczym Zawichoście w województwie świętokrzyskim. Zawodnicy mają do dyspozycji plany treningowe dostosowane do różnych poziomów zaawansowania, które pomagają optymalnie przygotować się do startu. Wydarzenie jest doskonałą okazją do sprawdzenia swojej formy na asfaltowej trasie o średnim stopniu trudności. Organizatorzy zapewniają wsparcie ekspertów oraz możliwość zarządzania informacjami o biegu poprzez platformę internetową.
course_highlights: Dystans 10 km na trasie asfaltowej
Trasa o średnim stopniu trudności
Malownicza lokalizacja w Zawichoście
additional: Dostępne plany treningowe od 8 do 20 tygodni, dostosowane do poziomu VDOT biegacza. Wsparcie ekspertów oraz możliwość korzystania z platformy do zarządzania wizytówką biegu i współpracy marketingowej.

name: VIII Nocny Bieg
description: VIII Otwarte Akademickie Mistrzostwa Łomży w nocnym biegu ulicznym to coroczna impreza organizowana przez Akademię Łomżyńską oraz Klub Uczelniany AZS Akademii Łomżyńskiej. Bieg odbywa się po ulicach Łomży, a jego celem jest upamiętnienie powstania Akademii oraz promocja aktywności fizycznej i zdrowego stylu życia. Zawodnicy mają do wyboru dystanse 5 km i 10 km, z atestem PZLA na trasie 10 km. Start następuje wieczorem, co nadaje biegowi wyjątkowy, nocny charakter.
course_highlights: Trasa 10 km z atestem PZLA
Bieg uliczny po Łomży
Limit czasu 1,5 godziny od startu
additional: Limit uczestników: 100 zawodników na 5 km i 100 na 10 km plus pula organizatora. Weryfikacja zawodników w Biurze Zawodów w dniu imprezy od 19:00 do 20:45. Zawodnicy muszą przebiec cały zadeklarowany dystans po asfalcie, skracanie trasy skutkuje dyskwalifikacją. Zmiany dystansów możliwe w dniu imprezy w namiocie pomiaru czasu.

name: XII Półmaraton Wierchami
description: XII Półmaraton Wierchami to górski bieg odbywający się w malowniczym Beskidzie Sądeckim, w okolicach Rytra. Trasa biegu prowadzi przez wymagające szlaki górskie z pięknymi widokami i znacznymi przewyższeniami, co stanowi prawdziwe wyzwanie dla biegaczy górskich. Impreza organizowana jest przez Stowarzyszenie Visegrad Maraton i przyciąga miłośników biegów ultra oraz krótszych dystansów. Uczestnicy mogą wybrać spośród kilku tras o różnej długości i stopniu trudności.
course_highlights: Trasa górska z dużymi przewyższeniami (np. +1124 m / -1124 m na dystansie 30 km)
Przebieg przez Beskid Sądecki z punktami odżywczymi na trasie
Widoki na szczyty takie jak Wielki Rogacz i Radziejowa
additional: Starty biegów odbywają się w Ośrodku Ryterski. Dystans Corno Owca 11 km startuje o godzinie 12:00, a Waligóra 30 km o godzinie 9:00. Trasy prowadzą przez oznakowane szlaki górskie z punktami odżywczymi. Pakiet startowy jest zapewniany dla osób zapisanych i opłaconych do określonego terminu. Możliwość płatności przez DotPay lub w biurze zawodów.

name: XIX Bieg O Błękitną Wstęgę
description: XIX Międzynarodowy Bieg o Błękitną Wstęgę to coroczne wydarzenie organizowane przez Stargardzki Klub Lekkoatletyczny, które od 19 lat promuje zdrowie, sprawność i pozytywną energię. Bieg główny odbywa się nocą, co nadaje mu wyjątkowy klimat, a trasa prowadzi ulicami Stargardu, pozwalając podziwiać najpiękniejsze zabytki miasta w blasku księżyca. To doskonała okazja do aktywnego spędzenia czasu i budowania wytrzymałości fizycznej oraz mentalnej. Organizatorzy zapraszają zarówno amatorów, jak i osoby z doświadczeniem sportowym do wspólnego świętowania ruchu i zdrowego stylu życia.
course_highlights: Nocny bieg z klimatem o godz. 21:00
Trasa startuje z Amfiteatru i prowadzi wokół Klejnotu Pomorza
Widoki na najpiękniejsze zabytki Stargardu w blasku księżyca
additional: Bieg odbywa się nocą, co tworzy niepowtarzalny klimat. Trasa biegu jest przygotowywana tak, aby umożliwić podziwianie zabytków Stargardu. Organizatorzy zachęcają do budowania wytrzymałości fizycznej i mentalnej przed biegiem. Wydarzenie ma charakter międzynarodowy i jest organizowane przez Stargardzki Klub Lekkoatletyczny.

name: Wrocławska Dycha
description: Wrocławska Dycha to coroczne zawody biegowe organizowane we Wrocławiu, oferujące dystanse 5 i 10 km. Bieg przyciąga zarówno amatorów, jak i bardziej doświadczonych biegaczy, zapewniając sportową atmosferę i możliwość rywalizacji na malowniczych trasach miasta. Impreza jest doskonałą okazją do aktywnego spędzenia czasu i integracji środowiska biegowego Wrocławia.
course_highlights: Trasy o długości 5 i 10 km w centrum Wrocławia
Malownicze miejskie krajobrazy
Przyjazna atmosfera dla biegaczy na różnych poziomach zaawansowania

name: X Bieg Pamięci Powstań Śląskich
location: Góra Świętej Anny, Leśnica, Opole Voivodeship, Polska

name: Heuchelheimer Mitternachtslauf
description: The Heuchelheim Midnight Run is a long-standing running event in Heuchelheim. It offers various distances for Bambini, students, recreational runners, relays, and the 10-kilometer main race. The course runs through the streets of Heuchelheim and includes some hills, particularly on Mühlberg. All participants receive medals and certificates, and registration is mainly through the MyRaceResult portal. The event is suitable for both individual and relay participants and has a family-friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: 600 m lap with a gentle incline on Brauhausstraße
2,500 m lap with a significant incline on Mühlberg (approx. 150 m)
10 km main race consisting of four laps of the 2.5 km course
additional: On the event day, late registration is possible from 17:30 until half an hour before the respective start. Advance registration is recommended for the relay race; late registration is only possible until one hour before the start. Timing is by transponder. Certificates can be printed out via MyRaceResult. Course description, registration via MyRaceResult, entry fees, transponder timing, refreshments, awards ceremony, showers, age categories, start times, awards, liability notice

name: 19. Burgberglauf Gehrden
price_range: 3 € pro Kind für Bambini- und Kinderläufe, sonst keine Angaben
description: The Burgberglauf 2026 takes place on June 20 in Gehrden and offers runners a choice of distances on a challenging 3.3 km loop with around 50 metres of elevation gain. The course passes through woodland and open farmland and requires a good level of fitness. Children under 12 have a separate, flat out-and-back course, while the Bambini runners start on shorter loops around the sports field. The event is family-friendly and, in addition to the races, offers a raffle with attractive prizes as well as refreshments for spectators and participants.
course_highlights: Challenging 3.3 km loop with approximately 50 metres of elevation gain
Course passes through woodland and open farmland
Separate, flat out-and-back course for children under 12
additional: Start and finish at the sports field of Matthias-Claudius-Gymnasium, Knülweg 10, 30989 Gehrden. Changing rooms and showers are available in the sports hall. Parking is not available in the event area. Race bib collection from 11:00 a.m. in the sports hall. Fully electronic timing via a chip attached to the shoe; return the chip after finishing (a €10 fee applies if it is lost). Raffle with attractive prizes; the grand prize is a pizza oven. The Bambini races (300 m and 700 m) start from 2:00 p.m. Bambini entries are also accepted on site on race day (€3, cash only). Refreshments for spectators include bratwurst, drinks and ice cream. Course: challenging 3.3 km loop, woodland trails, paved; online registration only; race bibs collected in the sports hall; no parking in the event area; Bambini races have no placings and include a medal.

name: Abendlauf TSV Blau-Weiß Ippinghausen
description: The TSV Blau-Weiß Ippinghausen Evening Run takes place in Wolfhagen-Ippinghausen. The event offers 10 km, half marathon, and marathon races on firm, paved forest paths, starting and finishing at Weidelsburg Stadium. The course runs through the town forest, including scenic sections such as Stöcketeich, and has several aid stations. The event is open to all age groups and offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with certificates for all participants.
course_highlights: 21 km loop for the half marathon; the marathon covers the loop twice
Start and finish at Weidelsburg Stadium, with a scenic loop through the town forest
Several aid stations (4 for the half marathon, 9 for the marathon); showers and changing rooms available
additional: Spikes are not allowed in any weather conditions. Start times are staggered by age group, from 16:30 (Bambini) to 17:00 (10 km/half marathon/marathon). Every participant receives a certificate. Parking is available at the sports ground, Waldecker Straße, and Vor dem Busche. HLV insurance covers all participants, including non-club members. Courses are on firm forest paths and the sports ground; spikes are not permitted. Registration via Raceresult; insurance provided by HLV.

name: Die 49. Nacht von Borgholzhausen
description: The Night of Borgholzhausen is a special running event held in the town centre of Borgholzhausen. From the Bambini Run and Schoolrunning to the atmospheric 10 km night run, there is something for all ages and ability levels. The event is known for its unique atmosphere, created by live music, cheerleaders, DJs and torches along the route. Teams, beginners and ambitious runners can enjoy an unforgettable evening filled with community spirit and a passion for running.
course_highlights: Paved streets through the town centre of Borgholzhausen
Cheerleaders, live music and DJs creating a lively atmosphere along the route
Torch-lit route and garden parties along the course
additional: The event starts with the Bambini Run at 18:00 (300 m, untimed, registration through kindergartens). This is followed by two Schoolrunning races: one for primary school pupils (approx. 1.6 km) and one for secondary school pupils (approx. 3 km). The company run (5 km) and the 5 km run are suitable for beginners and teams. The highlight is the 10 km night run, which is enlivened by a special atmosphere, with plenty of spectators and music. Individual registration is available online until shortly before the final start at 21:30. Various running distances, a running course for beginners, an atmosphere with music and torches, online registration

name: Nordholzer Windmühlenlauf
price_range: Kinder/Jugendliche/Wanderer/Walker 4,00 Euro; Erwachsene 8,00 Euro; Halbmarathon 12,00 Euro; Nachmeldung 2,00 Euro
description: The Nordholz Windmill Run is a long-standing running event in Wurster North Sea Coast offering various distances for children, young people and adults. The courses follow measured road routes officially recognised by the German Athletics Association (DLV). There are also hiking and walking options open to all age groups. The event has a family-friendly atmosphere, and every participant receives a medal and certificate.
course_highlights: Measured road courses with DLV certification
Distances from the 400 m Bambini run to the half marathon (21.0975 km)
Competition at Willi-Wicke Sports Ground, serving as the start and finish area
additional: Race-pack collection from 14:00 at the clubhouse at Willi-Wicke Sports Ground. Timing is by transponder, loaned with the race pack (20 euro fee if not returned). Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available at the start/finish area. The Bambini run is free, and accompaniment is permitted but not timed. The 5 km race counts as the district championship. Late entries are possible up to 1 hour before the start for an additional fee. Every participant receives a medal and certificate; walkers and hikers receive a certificate of participation. Courses are measured; timing is by transponder; changing rooms, showers and toilets are available; district championship on the 5 km course.

name: Samstagslauf Großenmeer
description: The Großenmeer Saturday Run is a long-standing grassroots running event, taking place for the 15th time. Organized by Großenmeerer Turnverein 1921 e.V., it offers a sporting opportunity for runners from the region and beyond. The event is open to various distances and welcomes all age groups. Registration is available via Laufmanager.net, and the organizers look forward to welcoming numerous participants.
course_highlights: A variety of routes for different ability levels
A run through the scenic region around Großenmeer and Ovelgönne
A traditional event with a friendly atmosphere and strong regional ties
additional: The run is organized by Großenmeerer Turnverein 1921 e.V., which also supports other sporting activities in the region. No start times or pricing tiers are explicitly listed on the website. The event is part of the Ovelgönne-Jade sports association. Routes, online registration, various running distances, regional sports activities

name: 3. Schluchthof Backyard Ultra
description: The 3rd Schluchthof Backyard Ultra takes place in Kleinostheim on the Main, near Aschaffenburg. This lovingly organized, private backyard ultra race emphasizes a family atmosphere and a small field of participants, so every lap is run together. The event offers a distinctive setting in a green corner between the Rhine-Main region and the Spessart, with runners setting off hour after hour until only one runner remains.

name: 41. Volkslauf in Baunatal
description: The 41st Baunatal Fun Run is a mass-participation sporting event with the motto “Baunatal Runs,” open to everyone regardless of club membership. The running routes are mostly on paved paths and largely through wooded areas. The 5 km route is an out-and-back course, while the shorter races, from 200 m to 1,000 m, take place in Parkstadion. The event is part of the Nordhessencup, a popular running series in the region.

name: Hennigsdorfer Feuerwehr- und Bahnenlauf
description: The Hennigsdorf Fire Service and Railways Run is a sporting event in Hennigsdorf, held annually in June at the OSZ sports ground. A range of races from 400 m to 5 km, including a fun run, children’s race, Nordic walking and a HandiCap race, offers suitable competitions for all ages and ability levels. The event is organised by the Stahl track and field athletes and also attracts runners from the volunteer fire service and the Berlin Fire Service. Entertainment and refreshments are provided, along with a children’s obstacle course, emergency vehicles, medical cover by the DLRG and an information stand.
course_highlights: Various distances from 400 m to 5 km
Start and finish at the OSZ sports ground in Hennigsdorf
Participation by fire service runners and a varied supporting programme
additional: Medals and certificates for all finishers. Event hours: approximately 8:30 to 14:30. Supporting programme with a children’s obstacle course, fire service emergency vehicles and medical cover by the DLRG. Refreshments for participants, volunteers and spectators.

name: Suderburger Abendlauf
description: The Suderburg Evening Run is a recreational sporting event for the whole family, held annually in June in Suderburg since 2022. The races run through the heathland and surrounding forests of the Lüneburg Heath on sandy, all-weather forest and farm tracks. In addition to traditional individual races, there is also a 3 x 1.9 km relay. The start and finish are at the sports ground on Tannrähm, and the event is attracting growing numbers of participants.

name: Fuffy Twister - From Dusk Till Dawn
description: The Fuffy Twister - From Dusk Till Dawn is a 50 km trail ultra in Langenhagen, Germany. It starts at night and has an 8-hour time limit. The race takes place in June and features straightforward organization, a low entry fee, an on-site finisher medal, and results and certificates published online. The small field makes it a more local and challenging test of endurance. The route runs along the northern edge of Hanover, near Hanover Airport, through the Bissendorfer Moor and Kananoher Forst, over varied terrain with moderate elevation gain.

name: Babenberger Volkslauf
description: The Babenberger Volkslauf is a family-friendly scenic run that has been held on the Saturday of the Kirchweih festival at St. Urban in Bamberg since 1999. The event offers running enthusiasts a wonderful opportunity to meet in a friendly atmosphere and run together for a good cause. The start and finish are at St. Urban Church, and the event supports social projects in the district each year. The organizers look forward to welcoming many participants and putting on a successful event.
